rationale: ROUND 4 on 25cd3044. Round 3's gating objections were both defects in MY SUBMISSION, not the code, and they were right: my edit-3 sketch showed the round-2 and round-3 newDeliveryEngine definitions side by side (which as sketched does not compile), because I had APPENDED the new sketch to the old instead of replacing it; and the wiring test my whole round-3 argument rested on never appeared in the test edit's sketch. Every sketch in this round is REWRITTEN WHOLESALE FROM THE COMMITTED FILES, none is an accumulation. SINCE ROUND 3 the code also changed, because an independent adversarial review (a fresh-context reviewer with read-only access, run 2026-08-26 at the user's request) found two real defects in the listener that three council rounds and I had missed, both now fixed in commit 67f1794f9 and included here: (1) THE POD COULD STAY READY WITH A DEAD CUSTOMER DOOR — both listener goroutines' cancel() calls were dead code; main blocked on a bare <-sigCh and nothing consumed the cancellation, so a bind failure logged once and the box would 502 every customer link with nothing unhealthy anywhere in the cluster. My round-2 answer to guardian's HIGH asserted the opposite of what the code did, which I state plainly rather than smooth over. The shutdown path is now select{sigCh, ctx.Done()}, making both cancels real — including the main listener's identical pre-existing dead one. (2) THE BOX-SHAPE GUARD VOUCHED FOR /d/ — assertRoutesAreBoxServable accepted any deliveryRoutePrefixes entry while the vhost proxies /c/ ONLY, so a /d/:token route registered before the vhost gains its block would pass every test and 404 at the box for every customer: the exact failure the assertion exists to prevent, deferred and then invisible. Fixed by splitting boxServablePrefixes (/c/ only — the guard now REFUSES /d/:token until the vhost block and the list entry land in one commit) from deliveryRoutePrefixes (admin-router guard, correctly keeps /d/). Both fixes mutation-proved. editquality's round-3 LOW on /d/ being speculative is answered by the same split: /d/ in the ADMIN-router guard costs nothing and refuses a premature download route on the wrong port; /d/ is no longer vouched for as servable anywhere.

plan.summary: ROUND 4. Core unchanged since round 1: the delivery routes MOVE off core-manager's admin router onto a second listener (opt-in server.delivery_port, unsafe default OFF), enforced by construction-time assertions over the REAL route tables. THIS ROUND: every sketch rewritten wholesale from the committed files (round 3's gating objections were sketch-accumulation artifacts — two conflicting newDeliveryEngine definitions shown side by side, and the load-bearing wiring test absent from the test edit). PLUS two fixes from an independent adversarial review, commit 67f1794f9: the shutdown path now consumes cancel() (select on sigCh + ctx.Done() — previously a listener bind failure left the pod Ready forever with the customer door dead, and my round-2 answer to guardian asserted the opposite), and the box-shape guard no longer vouches for /d/ (boxServablePrefixes = /c/ only, split from the admin-router guard's list; registering /d/:token refuses to start core-manager until the vhost's /d/ block lands in the same commit). Deployment half unchanged from round 3.

edits.rationale: ROUND 4: this edit GREW, because adversarial review proved my round-2/3 claim about it false. The goroutine and its cancel() were already here — but cancel() was DEAD: main blocked on a bare <-sigCh and nothing consumed the cancellation, so a delivery listener that failed to bind logged one error and the pod stayed Ready forever (the readiness probe reads /health on the ADMIN port), the box 502ing every customer link with nothing unhealthy in the cluster. Exactly guardian's round-2 worry, which I answered with 'it brings the service down' — asserted, not true. The shutdown select's ctx.Done() arm now makes every cancel() real, including the main listener's identical pre-existing dead one; exiting turns quietly-broken into a restart loop somebody sees.

THE EDIT EDITQUALITY'S 'missing' ITEM ASKED FOR — also already in the commit, also omitted from round 1's plan. editquality is exactly right that without it /c/ 404s indefinitely rather than transiently. It is a box file applied by the owner's box steps rather than by any deploy this repo runs, so it ships with a DO-NOT-APPLY-BEFORE-THE-ROLL header carrying the ancestry check: port 8090 does not answer until a core-manager image built from this commit runs, and applying early breaks every customer link at the box where there is no log line to find. Being LATE is harmless — until it is applied the box still proxies to 8088 where the routes no longer are, so /c/ 404s either way until both halves are in place, and customer_access_tokens = 0 means nobody can be holding a link.

edits.symbol: server.go: routes off the admin router; assertNoDeliveryRoutes; boxServablePrefixes + assertRoutesAreBoxServable; newDeliveryEngine/newDeliveryServer via the registrar seam
edits.rationale: ONE definition of everything, sketched from the committed file (commits a9b18a44c, f24743358, 67f1794f9). Two guards with distinct jobs: assertNoDeliveryRoutes keeps customer paths (and capturing wildcards) off the ADMIN router — fail-closed at construction; assertRoutesAreBoxServable keeps every route ON the delivery listener servable through the box's anchored regex — exact-match <prefix>:token, and only for prefixes the vhost actually proxies (boxServablePrefixes = /c/ only; /d/ is refused until the vhost gains its block, in the same commit as the list entry). newDeliveryEngine takes a small registrar interface purely so a test can hand it a violating route table and prove the assertion is WIRED — unwiring it once left the whole suite green. GET/POST parity falls out of the exact-match rule, which is what the second-click design needs: the METHOD is the security distinction, so the path must be identical.

THE DEFECT THIS BUILD ALREADY CAUGHT, recorded rather than smoothed over. server.delivery_port is set only by core-manager's production overlay and named in no service's YAML. viper's Unmarshal populates from viper's known key set, and AutomaticEnv alone does not add a key absent from both the config file and the defaults — so without an explicit BindEnv the env var is silently ignored, the listener never starts, and every customer link 404s at the box with the overlay reading perfectly correct and no error anywhere in the cluster. I wrote the test before the bind and it FAILED, which is the only reason this is a paragraph rather than a live outage. Binding affects no other service: unset stays empty, which is the OFF default.

edits.symbol: the test file: nine tests, seven mutations run, ALL killed (incl. the wiring test round 3's sketch omitted)
edits.rationale: Round 3's HIGH was exact: my grounded_in leaned on TestNewDeliveryEngineRefusesAnUnservableRouteTable and the sketch never showed it. It is here now, with the full mutation table. That test exists because unwiring assertRoutesAreBoxServable once left this whole suite green — the direct-call tests proved the function worked and nothing proved anything called it; the registrar seam makes the wiring itself falsifiable. The /d/ expectation FLIPPED with the boxServable split: a /d/:token route must now be REFUSED as box-servable (the vhost has no /d/ block) while still being refused on the admin router — a paired assertion keeps the two guards' distinct jobs honest.

ROUND 1 OBJECTIONS ANSWERED BY CHECKS RUN THIS ROUND, not by argument. reuse_agent asked whether an existing 'second constrained listener' or route-audit pattern exists. IT DOES, and I found it: `platform/health/server.go` is a shared second-listener helper, and five adapters (analyser, git, browserrunner, webscrape, thunder) each hand-roll a `healthServer`. platform/health is NOT usable here and the reasons are structural, not preference: it is gorilla/mux (the delivery handler takes a gin.IRouter), it ALWAYS mounts /health and /ready — which would break the delivery-only property this listener exists to have, and which my own mutation #3 proves the tests catch — it retains no *http.Server so it cannot drain a customer mid-click, and Start() also launches a metrics listener. Extending it would mean changing a helper five live adapters depend on, to make it serve a case it was not built for.

REUSE, THE SECOND HALF: there IS an existing house convention for route-table assertions and I independently matched it rather than inventing one — `internal/tools-api/api/server_test.go` iterates r.Routes() to assert registration, to prove a route is not shadowed, and (TestGripperGroupIsOptIn) to assert that an OPT-IN feature registers NO routes when its config is nil. That last one is the same assertion shape as my TestDeliveryListenerIsOptInAndDefaultsOff. So the convention exists as TESTS, not as a shared helper, and this change follows it.
